6. Environmental Impacts of the Proposed Improvement.
The largest effect to the human environment by the freeway proposal would be the acquisition of lands for the necessary right of way and the relocation of families and businesses. Land acquisitions for the new cargo area as part of General Mitchell's expansion program has already made its impact on the surrounding area. Land acquisition for the project within the recommended Corridor No. 5 was proceeding under an approved Relocation Plan. Nine families and two businesses remain to be relocated.
General Mitchell Field has already generated land uses around its periphery. Commercial enterprises serving air passengers, air cargo and airlines as well as industries that transport materials by truck and by air have been attracted by the airport facilities. Recent commercial and residential land developments along the local street system have not been discouraged by this growth nor have the municipalities zoned against it. The City of Milwaukee is presently in the land bank business and is promoting additional commercial and industrial growth for the area. As a result of this growth, the existing surface street system in the vicinity of the airport is currently congested. The system provides local land access, business and industrical access, as well as high speed thru traffic with a good portion oriented to the airport.
The remaining undeveloped lands in the vicinity of the airport are rapidly being developed for residential and commercial development.
